nodes.title: Riemann Hypothesis
nodes.statement: Every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part 1/2 (Mathlib `RiemannHypothesis`; repository alias `VFMidRiemannHypothesisStatement`).
nodes.notes: No route in this registry closes RH; every RH path below lists its unpaid inputs.

nodes.title: von Koch prime-counting criterion (1901)
nodes.statement: RH <=> pi(x) - Li(x) = O(sqrt(x) log x). von Koch (1901) proved RH => pi(x) = Li(x) + O(sqrt(x) log x); the converse is the classical Mellin/partial-summation argument (an O(x^(1/2+eps)) error continues the relevant Dirichlet series to Re s > 1/2). Li_2(x) = int_2^x dt/log t differs from li(x) by the constant li(2) = 1.04516..., so the criterion is normalization-independent.
nodes.normalization: Either li or Li_2; the additive constant li(2) is absorbed in the O(sqrt(x) log x) scale.
literature: H. von Koch, "Sur la distribution des nombres premiers", Acta Mathematica 24 (1901), 159-182, doi:10.1007/BF02403071 (RH => error bound).
does_not_prove: Any arithmetic estimate on actual primes

nodes.title: ClassicalVonKochRHCriterion (explicit Lean interface)
nodes.statement: structure ClassicalVonKochRHCriterion where iff_riemannHypothesis : PrimeLiVonKochBoundedStatement <-> VFMidRiemannHypothesisStatement. Supplied as an explicit theorem argument; the repository does not construct it.
literature: Packages HISTORICAL-VONKOCH-1901 in the repository's Li_2 normalization.
does_not_prove: The classical analytic theorem inside Lean (it is a hypothesis, not a construction)
nodes.notes: `#print axioms` does not report this structure: it is an ordinary theorem argument, not a logical axiom.

nodes.title: Formalize or import the classical von Koch criterion
nodes.statement: Construct a term of ClassicalVonKochRHCriterion, either from an existing certified Lean proof of the classical equivalence or by a new proof in the pinned Lean 4.34.1 / Mathlib toolchain.
literature: HISTORICAL-VONKOCH-1901; Mathlib (pinned) does not expose this equivalence in the Li_2 normalization (comment on ClassicalVonKochRHCriterion).
does_not_prove: OPEN-VF-ACTUAL-PRIME: discharging the interface leaves the actual-prime estimate exactly as open as before
nodes.notes: Formalization-completeness objective only. It is not a new conjecture and does not substitute for the open arithmetic estimate OPEN-VF-ACTUAL-PRIME.

nodes.title: Canonical square-block VF definition
nodes.statement: vfCanonical x = vfMid x + sqrt 2; for x >= 4, R = floor(sqrt x): VF_can(x) = sqrt2 + sum_{r=2}^{R-1} (2r+1)/log(r^2+r+1/2) + (x-R^2)/log((R^2+x)/2). The square-endpoint defect obeys the exact actual-prime recurrence D_{R+1} = D_R + (P_R - V_R).
does_not_prove: Pointwise optimality of the sqrt2 phase

nodes.title: Root-scale VF/Li_2 quadrature (pre-#932)
nodes.statement: VFMidLiRootBoundedStatement: exists B >= 0, forall x >= 4, |vfMid(x) - Li_2(x)| <= B sqrt(x). This is the quadrature input actually used by the von Koch equivalence proofs.

nodes.title: VF_can - Li_2 = O(1) on the whole real continuum
nodes.statement: exists C, forall real x >= 4: |VF_can(x) - Li_2(x)| <= C (and |vfMid(x) - Li_2(x)| <= C_square + C_live). Unconditional; elementary uniform midpoint quadrature, no prime-distribution hypothesis.
does_not_prove: Any bound on pi - VF_can or pi - Li_2
nodes.notes: Strictly stronger than the root-scale quadrature MILESTONE-VF-LI-ROOT that the von Koch equivalence consumes; either suffices for the reduction.

nodes.title: Canonical VF square endpoint <=> classical prime-Li von Koch bound
nodes.statement: (exists C >= 0, forall R >= 2, |pi(R^2) - VF_can(R^2)| <= C R log R) <=> (exists C' >= 0, forall real x >= 4, |pi(x) - Li_2(x)| <= C' sqrt(x) log x), and both are equivalent to the all-real canonical and legacy vfMid forms, with renormalized nonnegative constants.
does_not_prove: The independent classical von Koch-to-RH analytic theorem (IFACE-CLASSICAL-VONKOCH is an explicit argument)

nodes.notes: Equivalent (MILESTONE-VONKOCH-VF-LEAN) to the classical prime-Li von Koch bound, hence RH-equivalent given HISTORICAL-VONKOCH-1901. Known baseline from imported 7/8: D_can(R) = O(R^(7/4+eps)).
